## Design

### 2026-10-08 – Today was my first session working on my Hack Club Half Life project, **Orion** — my idea for an advanced Windows-compatible mechanical keyboard.

**0.5h**

Today was my first session working on my Hack Club Half Life project, **Orion** — my idea for an advanced Windows-compatible mechanical keyboard.

I started by thinking about what I actually wanted from a keyboard beyond the normal keys. I came up with ideas like a built-in joystick, a second WASD cluster, a second set of arrow keys, mouse buttons, a rotary encoder for scrolling, media controls, dedicated shortcut keys for ChatGPT, Discord, Instagram and World Chess, and lots of RGB lighting.

I then used ChatGPT to turn these ideas into an initial physical design concept. I generated the first concept images to visualize how all the controls could fit together while still keeping the keyboard looking clean and futuristic.

![Orion Neon Command Keyboard Blueprint](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/EmbFv8sT4oiWItMJ6FVW7tjawx6AuYDp/50c35d7af556092432a10b2a3a10a44a75da40c48332b61cc619a462639e2d76.png)

![ORION RGB Gaming Keyboard Concept](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/EmbFv8sT4oiWItMJ6FVW7tjawx6AuYDp/85cd29c41ba60ff0f9c6e408c47c520786e342d60e026b4bdaa2cbaf63635b10.png)

This is only the first design, so I expect the layout and features to change as I learn more about PCB design and figure out what is actually practical to build.

I'm really excited to move forward with Orion and start turning the concept into a real PCB.

### 2026-10-09 – Today, I moved from the initial concept of Orion to creating my first 3D model of the keyboard. The goal was to start visualising how all the different components would fit together in a real physical

**3.5h**

Today, I moved from the initial concept of Orion to creating my first 3D model of the keyboard. The goal was to start visualising how all the different components would fit together in a real physical design.

I created the initial layout, including the main keyboard, navigation cluster, numpad, secondary WASD and arrow-key clusters, and the built-in joystick. I also started incorporating the raised display bar at the top with the ORION branding.

This gave me a much clearer idea of the keyboard's overall proportions and how its additional controls could be arranged while retaining the familiar full-size keyboard layout.

**Here is the current 3D model of Orion:**

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/EmbFv8sT4oiWItMJ6FVW7tjawx6AuYDp/64a3d2acfb46706d4e5dd3025e8b544345921352e3c8f1c5ea93228c4c5b04a5.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/EmbFv8sT4oiWItMJ6FVW7tjawx6AuYDp/586041cc0845a1db5a46c1890eb64799fd8cd23a37377e0f93f11a198943f530.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/EmbFv8sT4oiWItMJ6FVW7tjawx6AuYDp/67f308dbf207fa9b5e9e71a22f3bc5a50260ca45bab8c75201ce147f1b664c16.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/EmbFv8sT4oiWItMJ6FVW7tjawx6AuYDp/e30da24ce0cc26227390104febb558ca6f8212ce1d51071780c36a67e916d85f.png)

This is still an early prototype, and there is plenty of room for improvement. My next steps are to refine the placement of the additional controls, incorporate the media buttons, mouse buttons and rotary encoder, and develop the RGB lighting and overall aesthetic.

I'm excited to keep improving the model and eventually turn this design into a functional custom PCB!

### 2026-10-11 – After developing the initial concept and rough mechanical layout for Orion, I moved on to the electronics architecture required to bring the keyboard to life.

**4.5h**

After developing the initial concept and rough mechanical layout for Orion, I moved on to the electronics architecture required to bring the keyboard to life.

I selected the Raspberry Pi Pico as the main controller and planned to use two MCP23017 I/O expanders to handle the large number of keys in the keyboard matrix. The design also incorporates individual key-switch diodes, an analog joystick, a rotary encoder, dedicated media and shortcut buttons, an I²C OLED display, and addressable RGB lighting.

I worked on assigning GPIO pins, defining the row-and-column connections for the key matrix, and planning the communication between the controller and its peripherals. I also considered the separate 5 V power requirements of the RGB LEDs, including a fuse, bulk capacitor, and a 74AHCT125 level shifter to interface the LED data signal safely with the 5 V LEDs.

I used Schematik to document the component connections and develop the firmware for keyboard input, mouse controls, media functions, and custom shortcuts. This stage helped me identify the importance of checking pin assignments, USB HID compatibility, power requirements, and firmware behaviour rather than relying on the circuit diagram alone.

**Current progress:** The electronics architecture and firmware are being developed, and I am deploying the updated project to check whether the firmware compiles successfully. The next step is to resolve any remaining issues, verify the schematic, and work towards a PCB design that can be tested in practice.

The goal is to turn Orion from a concept into a functional, programmable keyboard with integrated gaming controls and custom features.

The schematik.io project is available at https://www.schematik.io/projects/advanced-gaming-keyboard-vrfv

### 2026-10-11 – Orion is now in the final stages of its electronics design! The core architecture, component selection, GPIO assignments, key-matrix connections, auxiliary controls, and RGB lighting arrangement have

**5h**

Orion is now in the final stages of its electronics design! The core architecture, component selection, GPIO assignments, key-matrix connections, auxiliary controls, and RGB lighting arrangement have been documented.

I have also refined the firmware to support dedicated media controls, application shortcuts, a complete numeric-keypad implementation, joystick input, and mouse functions. The project documentation now includes the Bill of Materials (BOM) and schematics/connection details, which I am attaching for review.

The major design decisions are in place, and I am currently checking the remaining details to ensure the electronics and firmware work together as intended. I am also checking the deployment result and addressing any final issues before wrapping up this stage.

Orion is almost ready for its final submission. I will submit the final design shortly after completing the remaining verification and documentation checks, bringing the project one step closer to PCB implementation and eventual hardware testing.

### 2026-10-11 – The electronics design phase of Orion is now complete for this submission milestone!

**15h**

The electronics design phase of Orion is now complete for this submission milestone!

I have documented the circuit architecture, component connections, controller pin assignments, key-matrix design, auxiliary controls, and RGB power arrangement. I have also updated the firmware to support the keyboard's dedicated media controls, application shortcuts, numeric keypad, joystick, and mouse functions.

I have attached the Bill of Materials (BOM) and schematics/connection documentation to provide a clearer picture of the components used and how the different subsystems are intended to work together.

This marks an important step in moving Orion from a concept into a concrete electronics design. The next stage is to confirm the final firmware build, validate the electrical connections, and continue towards PCB layout and hardware testing.

Orion is designed to be more than a conventional keyboard: it brings together programmable typing, gaming controls, media functions, RGB lighting, and custom shortcuts in one integrated system.
